service:
You can use Amazon CloudWatch Observability Admin to discover and understand the state of telemetry configuration in CloudWatch for your Amazon Web Services Organization or account. This simplifies the process of auditing your telemetry collection configurations across multiple resource types within your Amazon Web Services Organization or account. By providing a consolidated view, it allows you to easily review and manage telemetry settings, helping you ensure proper monitoring and data collection across your Amazon Web Services environment. For more information, see Auditing CloudWatch telemetry conﬁgurations in the CloudWatch User Guide.

For information on the permissions you need to use this API, see Identity and access management for Amazon CloudWatch in the CloudWatch User Guide.

operations.CreateCentralizationRuleForOrganization: Creates a centralization rule that applies across an Amazon Web Services Organization. This operation can only be called by the organization's management account or a delegated administrator account.
operations.CreateConnector: Creates a connector to a third-party cloud provider. With a connector, you can discover resources in the provider and collect their telemetry. Currently, Microsoft Azure is the only supported provider.
operations.CreateDatasetIntegration:
Creates a dataset integration for the caller's account in the current region and returns its ARN.

To use this operation, you must have permission to access the dataset integration resources through the IAM role specified in the RoleArn parameter.

If a dataset integration already exists for the account, this operation fails with a ConflictException.
operations.CreateS3TableIntegration: Creates an integration between CloudWatch and S3 Tables for analytics. This integration enables querying CloudWatch telemetry data using analytics engines like Amazon Athena, Amazon Redshift, and Apache Spark.
operations.CreateTelemetryPipeline: Creates a telemetry pipeline for processing and transforming telemetry data. The pipeline defines how data flows from sources through processors to destinations, enabling data transformation and delivering capabilities.
operations.CreateTelemetryRule: Creates a telemetry rule that defines how telemetry should be configured for Amazon Web Services resources in your account. The rule specifies which resources should have telemetry enabled and how that telemetry data should be collected based on resource type, telemetry type, and selection criteria.
operations.CreateTelemetryRuleForOrganization: Creates a telemetry rule that applies across an Amazon Web Services Organization. This operation can only be called by the organization's management account or a delegated administrator account.
operations.DeleteCentralizationRuleForOrganization: Deletes an organization-wide centralization rule. This operation can only be called by the organization's management account or a delegated administrator account.
operations.DeleteConnector: Deletes a connector and its telemetry manifest.
operations.DeleteDatasetIntegration: Deletes a dataset integration for the caller's account in the current region. This operation is idempotent; if you submit the same delete more than once, each call succeeds.
operations.DeleteS3TableIntegration: Deletes an S3 Table integration and its associated data. This operation removes the connection between CloudWatch Observability Admin and S3 Tables.
operations.DeleteTelemetryPipeline: Deletes a telemetry pipeline and its associated resources. This operation stops data processing and removes the pipeline configuration.
operations.DeleteTelemetryRule: Deletes a telemetry rule from your account. Any telemetry configurations previously created by the rule will remain but no new resources will be configured by this rule.
operations.DeleteTelemetryRuleForOrganization: Deletes an organization-wide telemetry rule. This operation can only be called by the organization's management account or a delegated administrator account.
operations.GetCentralizationRuleForOrganization: Retrieves the details of a specific organization centralization rule. This operation can only be called by the organization's management account or a delegated administrator account.
operations.GetConnectorTelemetryManifest: Retrieves the telemetry manifest of a connector and its current version. If the connector has no telemetry manifest, this operation returns a ResourceNotFoundException.
operations.GetConnectorTelemetrySetup: Generates the artifacts that you use to create the infrastructure in your cloud provider that delivers the telemetry declared in the connector's telemetry manifest. This operation doesn't change any resources in your cloud provider or in Amazon Web Services.
operations.GetDatasetIntegration: Returns the dataset integration for the caller's account in the current region.
operations.GetS3TableIntegration: Retrieves information about a specific S3 Table integration, including its configuration, status, and metadata.
operations.GetTelemetryEnrichmentStatus: Returns the current status of the resource tags for telemetry feature, which enhances telemetry data with additional resource metadata from Resource Explorer.
operations.GetTelemetryEvaluationStatus: Returns the current onboarding status of the telemetry config feature, including the status of the feature and reason the feature failed to start or stop.
operations.GetTelemetryEvaluationStatusForOrganizat: This returns the onboarding status of the telemetry configuration feature for the organization. It can only be called by a Management Account of an Amazon Web Services Organization or an assigned Delegated Admin Account of Amazon CloudWatch telemetry config.
operations.GetTelemetryPipeline: Retrieves information about a specific telemetry pipeline, including its configuration, status, and metadata.
operations.GetTelemetryRule: Retrieves the details of a specific telemetry rule in your account.
operations.GetTelemetryRuleForOrganization: Retrieves the details of a specific organization telemetry rule. This operation can only be called by the organization's management account or a delegated administrator account.
operations.GetThirdPartyTelemetryEnrichment: Returns the details of a third-party telemetry enrichment, including its status and source configuration.
operations.ListCentralizationRulesForOrganization: Lists all centralization rules in your organization. This operation can only be called by the organization's management account or a delegated administrator account.
operations.ListConnectors: Lists the connectors in the account and Region. This operation returns results in pages. To get the next page, pass the returned NextToken in the next call. We recommend that you use pagination to ensure that the operation returns quickly and successfully.
operations.ListDatasetIntegrations: Returns the dataset integrations in your account.
operations.ListResourceTelemetry: Returns a list of telemetry configurations for Amazon Web Services resources supported by telemetry config. For more information, see Auditing CloudWatch telemetry configurations.
operations.ListResourceTelemetryForOrganization: Returns a list of telemetry configurations for Amazon Web Services resources supported by telemetry config in the organization.
operations.ListResourcesByConnector: Lists resources in your cloud provider that the connector can access, such as management groups, subscriptions, resource types, Regions, resources, and Event Hubs. Use the results to build a telemetry manifest. This operation returns results in pages. To get the next page, pass the returned NextToken in the next call. We recommend that you use pagination to ensure that the operation returns quickly and successfully.
operations.ListS3TableIntegrations: Lists all S3 Table integrations in your account. We recommend using pagination to ensure that the operation returns quickly and successfully.
operations.ListTagsForResource: Lists all tags attached to the specified resource. Supports telemetry rule resources, telemetry pipeline resources, and third-party telemetry enrichment resources.
operations.ListTelemetryPipelines: Returns a list of telemetry pipelines in your account. Returns up to 100 results. If more than 100 telemetry pipelines exist, include the NextToken value from the response to retrieve the next set of results.
operations.ListTelemetryRules: Lists all telemetry rules in your account. You can filter the results by specifying a rule name prefix.
operations.ListTelemetryRulesForOrganization: Lists all telemetry rules in your organization. This operation can only be called by the organization's management account or a delegated administrator account.
operations.ListThirdPartyTelemetryEnrichments: Returns a summary of each third-party telemetry enrichment in your account and Region. To get the full configuration of an enrichment, use GetThirdPartyTelemetryEnrichment. The results are paginated. To get the next page of results, use NextToken.
operations.PutConnectorTelemetryManifest: Creates or replaces the telemetry manifest of a connector. The telemetry manifest declares which resources in your cloud provider to collect telemetry from and which telemetry types to collect. To avoid overwriting changes made by another caller, specify ExpectedVersion.
operations.StartTelemetryEnrichment: Enables the resource tags for telemetry feature for your account, which enhances telemetry data with additional resource metadata from Resource Explorer to provide richer context for monitoring and observability.
operations.StartTelemetryEvaluation: This action begins onboarding the caller Amazon Web Services account to the telemetry config feature.
operations.StartTelemetryEvaluationForOrganization: This actions begins onboarding the organization and all member accounts to the telemetry config feature.
operations.StartTelemetryPipelineRefresh:
Starts a refresh of an external-cloud telemetry pipeline. The refresh re-reads the connector's telemetry manifest and re-discovers the sources in scope.

The pipeline must be in the ACTIVE or UPDATE_FAILED state, with no refresh already running. You can use GetTelemetryPipeline to track the refresh.
operations.StartThirdPartyTelemetryEnrichment:
Starts a third-party telemetry enrichment. An enrichment adds resource metadata, such as tags, from a third-party telemetry source to the telemetry that CloudWatch receives from the resources of that source.

You specify an Amazon Web Services Config connector for your third-party environment, such as a Microsoft Azure tenant. You can use each connector for only one enrichment.

To use this operation, you must have the config:PutThirdPartyServiceLinkedConfigurationRecorder permission. If the Amazon Web Services Config service-linked role does not exist in your account, you must also have the iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole permission.
operations.StopTelemetryEnrichment: Disables the resource tags for telemetry feature for your account, stopping the enhancement of telemetry data with additional resource metadata.
operations.StopTelemetryEvaluation: This action begins offboarding the caller Amazon Web Services account from the telemetry config feature.
operations.StopTelemetryEvaluationForOrganization: This action offboards the Organization of the caller Amazon Web Services account from the telemetry config feature.
operations.StopThirdPartyTelemetryEnrichment:
Stops a third-party telemetry enrichment. CloudWatch stops adding resource metadata from the third-party telemetry source to your telemetry.

To use this operation, you must have the config:DeleteServiceLinkedConfigurationRecorder permission.
operations.TagResource: Adds or updates tags for a resource. Supports telemetry rule resources, telemetry pipeline resources, and third-party telemetry enrichment resources.
operations.TestTelemetryPipeline: Tests a pipeline configuration with sample records to validate data processing before deployment. This operation helps ensure your pipeline configuration works as expected.
operations.UntagResource: Removes tags from a resource. Supports telemetry rule resources, telemetry pipeline resources, and third-party telemetry enrichment resources.
operations.UpdateCentralizationRuleForOrganization: Updates an existing centralization rule that applies across an Amazon Web Services Organization. This operation can only be called by the organization's management account or a delegated administrator account.
operations.UpdateDatasetIntegration: Updates a dataset integration for the caller's account in the current region. This operation is idempotent; if you submit the same update more than once, each call succeeds.
operations.UpdateTelemetryPipeline:
Updates the configuration of an existing telemetry pipeline.

The following attributes cannot be updated after pipeline creation:

  • Pipeline name - The pipeline name is immutable

  • Pipeline ARN - The ARN is automatically generated and cannot be changed

  • Source type - Once a pipeline is created with a specific source type (such as S3, CloudWatch Logs, GitHub, or third-party sources), it cannot be changed to a different source type

Processors can be added, removed, or modified. However, some processors are not supported for third-party pipelines and cannot be added through updates.

Source-Specific Update Rules

CloudWatch Logs Sources (Vended and Custom)

Updatable: sts_role_arn

Fixed: data_source_name, data_source_type, sink (must remain @original)

S3 Sources (Crowdstrike, Zscaler, SentinelOne, Custom)

Updatable: All SQS configuration parameters, sts_role_arn, codec settings, compression type, bucket ownership settings, sink log group

Fixed: notification_type, aws.region

GitHub Audit Logs

Updatable: All Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager attributes, scope (can switch between ORGANIZATION/ENTERPRISE), organization or enterprise name, range, authentication credentials (PAT or GitHub App)

Microsoft Sources (Entra ID, Office365, Windows)

Updatable: All Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager attributes, tenant_id, workspace_id (Windows only), OAuth2 credentials (client_id, client_secret)

Okta Sources (SSO, Auth0)

Updatable: All Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager attributes, domain, range, OAuth2 credentials (client_id, client_secret)

Palo Alto Networks

Updatable: All Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager attributes, hostname, basic authentication credentials (username, password)

ServiceNow CMDB

Updatable: All Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager attributes, instance_url, range, OAuth2 credentials (client_id, client_secret)

Wiz CNAPP

Updatable: All Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager attributes, region, range, OAuth2 credentials (client_id, client_secret)

CentralizeWithDataProtection.base:
Specifies the data protection setting that a rule applies to the log events that it centralizes. If you don't specify a value, the rule centralizes the original log events. The following values are supported:

  • ENABLED – The rule centralizes masked log events.

  • DISABLED – The rule centralizes the original log events.

refs.SourceLogsConfiguration$CentralizeWithDa:
Specifies whether this centralization rule centralizes log events with data protection applied. If you don't specify this setting, or you set it to DISABLED, the rule centralizes the original log events, including any sensitive data that a data protection policy on the source log group masks.

When you set this to ENABLED, the rule centralizes the same masked data that anyone in the source account without the logs:Unmask permission sees. The rule doesn't copy the original values to the destination, so you can't unmask them in the destination account. The rule centralizes log events from source log groups that don't have a data protection policy without changes.

The setting applies only to log events that the rule centralizes after you enable it. It doesn't change log events that the rule already centralized.

If you use the same token with different parameters, including different tags, the service returns a ValidationException. This operation is idempotent when you use the same token and parameters.

The strategy for resolving tag conflicts between source and destination log groups.

  • ADD_ONLY – Only adds new tags from the source without modifying existing destination tags.

  • UPDATE_SYNC – Adds new tags and updates existing tags from the source. Does not remove destination tags that are absent from the source.

  • IN_SYNC – Keeps destination tags fully synchronized with source tags, including removing destination tags that do not exist on the source.

TelemetryPipelineConfiguration.base:
Defines the configuration for a pipeline, including how data flows from sources through processors to destinations. The configuration is specified in YAML format and must include a valid pipeline definition with required source and sink components. This pipeline enables end-to-end telemetry data collection, transformation, and delivery while supporting optional processing steps and extensions for enhanced functionality.

The primary pipeline configuration section are:

  • Source: Defines where log data originates from (S3 buckets, CloudWatch Logs, third-party APIs). Each pipeline must have exactly one source.

  • Processors (optional): Transform, parse, and enrich log data as it flows through the pipeline. Processors are applied sequentially in the order they are defined.

  • Sink: Defines the destination where processed log data is sent. Each pipeline must have exactly one sink.

  • Extensions (optional): Provide additional functionality such as Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager integration for credential management.

For more details on each configuration section see CloudWatch pipelines User Guide. Additional comprehensive configuration examples can be found in the CreateTelemetryPipeline API docs.
